SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Schedule D, Part X, Line 2 FIN 48 (ASC 740) footnote
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Foundation is exempt from federal and state income taxes under Section 501 (c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code and Section 23701(d) of the California Franchise Tax Code. Accordingly, no provision for current or deferred income tax expense is recorded in the financial statements. The Foundation adopted the provisions of FASB ASC Topic 740-10, "Income Taxes" regarding accounting for uncertain tax positions. Management is not aware of any tax positions that are more likely than not to change in the next 12 months, or that would sustain an examination by applicable taxing authorities. The Foundation recognizes accrued penalties and interest associated with uncertain tax positions as part of the statement of activities, when applicable. Management has determined that the Foundation has no uncertain tax positions at September 30, 2024 and therefore no amounts have been accrued. The federal and state income tax returns of the Foundation are subject to examination by the IRS and state taxing authorities, generally for three years after they are filed.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Schedule I, Part I, Line 2 Procedures for monitoring use of grant funds.
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE ORGANIZATION RAISES FUNDS ON BEHALF OF AND PROVIDES ASSISTANCE TO SHARP CORONADO HOSPITAL AND HEALTHCARE CENTER. THE FUNDS RAISED MAY BE RESTRICTED BY THE DONOR FOR A SPECIFIC PURPOSE OR MAY BE UNRESTRICTED. SHARP CORONADO HOSPITAL AND HEALTHCARE CENTER SUBMITS REQUESTS FOR SUPPORT BASED ON THE AVAILABILITY OF THESE SPECIFICALLY DESIGNATED FUNDS. THE ORGANIZATION MAY ALSO UTILIZE UNRESTRICTED FUNDS TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL SUPPORT. IN THESE INSTANCES, THE HOSPITAL SUBMITS PROPOSALS TO THE ORGANIZATION FOR REVIEW AND CONSIDERATION. THE ORGANIZATION'S MANAGEMENT AND GOVERNING BOARD REVIEW THE PROPOSALS AND DETERMINE WHICH TO FUND. THE HOSPITAL SUBMITS DOCUMENTATION VERIFYING COMPLETION AND PAYMENT OF THE PROJECT AND IS SUBSEQUENTLY REIMBURSED BY THE ORGANIZATION. ADDITIONALLY, THE MANAGEMENT TEAM EVALUATES REQUESTS FOR CONTRIBUTIONS FROM OUTSIDE ORGANIZATIONS TAKING INTO ACCOUNT HOW THEY ALIGN WITH THE ORGANIZATION'S MISSION.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part III, Line 1 Organization's Mission
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The corporation is a nonprofit public benefit corporation and is not organized for the private gain of any person. The specific purposes of the corporation are to (i) raise money, solicit donations, and disburse the principal and income therefrom at reasonable, regular intervals for the benefit of the Sharp Coronado Hospital and Healthcare Center, a California nonprofit public benefit corporation which is tax-exempt within the meaning of Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Hospital"); (ii) to hold title or a master leasehold interest in the real property (including the buildings) located at 250 Prospect Place, Coronado, California 92118 and used for hospital and related purposes (the real property and buildings are collectively referred to as "Facilities"); (iii) to lease the Facilities to Hospital, which will operate the Facilities for the benefit of the communities served by Hospital; (iv) and to pursue any and all charitable activities related to the foregoing specific purposes.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part V, Line 2a
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: PRIOR TO 1/1/2022 CORONADO HOSPITAL FOUNDATION EMPLOYEES' SALARIES AND WAGES WERE PAID UNDER SHARP CORONADO HOSPITAL AND HEALTHCARE CENTER'S TAX ID NUMBER (EIN 95-0651579), AND AS SUCH WERE ALSO REPORTED ON SHARP CORONADO HOSPITAL AND HEALTHCARE CENTER'S FORM 990. STARTING WITH 1/1/2022 CORONADO HOSPITAL FOUNDATION EMPLOYEES' SALARIES AND WAGES ARE PAID UNDER SHARP HEALTHCARE'S TAX ID NUMBER (EIN 95-6077327), AND AS SUCH ARE ALSO REPORTED ON SHARP HEALTHCARE'S FORM 990. Coronado Hospital Foundation does not directly employ individuals but leases all of its personnel from Sharp HealthCare, a related organization that exercises control over the foundation. These leased employees operate under the direction and supervision of Coronado Hospital Foundation and perform all essential functions necessary for the foundation's operations. Sharp HealthCare, as the common law employer, is responsible for all employment-related obligations, including the payment of wages, withholding and remittance of employment taxes, and the filing of all required federal employment tax returns (e.g., Form 941) under its own Employer Identification Number (EIN). Accordingly, Coronado Hospital Foundation has reported the number of leased employees on Line 2a. However, it answered "No" to Line 2b because it does not file the employment tax returns directly.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 13 PART VI, LINE 13
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: CORONADO HOSPITAL FOUNDATION ("CHF") IS OPERATED UNDER A MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT WITH SHARP HEALTHCARE FOUNDATION (FEIN 95-3492461). PER THE MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT, SHARP HEALTHCARE FOUNDATION IS TASKED WITH MANAGING THE DAY TO DAY OPERATIONS OF CHF INCLUDING THE ADMINISTRATION OF ALL POLICIES AND PROCEDURES. IN THE EVENT THE CHF DOES NOT HAVE A SPECIFIC POLICY THAT HAS BEEN ADOPTED BY CHF'S GOVERNING BODY, SHARP HEALTHCARE FOUNDATION ADMINISTERS THE POLICY UNDER WHICH IT IS GOVERNED. SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 12c Conflict of interest policy
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY IS DISTRIBUTED ANNUALLY TO THE ORGANIZATION'S DIRECTORS, PRINCIPAL OFFICER, AND MEMBERS OF COMMITTEES WITH BOARD DELEGATED POWERS. THE ORGANIZATION'S ADMINISTRATIVE STAFF CONFIRMS THAT ALL ANNUAL DISCLOSURES ARE COMPLETED AND RETURNED. INDIVIDUALS WHO FIND THEY MAY HAVE A CONFLICT OF INTEREST DUE TO A FINANCIAL INTEREST OR WHO MAY NOT OTHERWISE MEET THE REQUIREMENTS OF THE POLICY, SHALL IMMEDIATELY MAKE FULL WRITTEN DISCLOSURE OF THE NATURE AND DETAILS OF THE POTENTIAL CONFLICT TO THE OFFICERS, DIRECTORS AND MEMBERS OF COMMITTEES WITH BOARD DELEGATED POWERS CONSIDERING THE PROPOSED TRANSACTION OR ARRANGEMENT. AFTER DISCLOSURE TO THE BOARD OR COMMITTEE, OF THE FINANCIAL INTEREST AND AFTER DISCUSSION WITH THE BOARD OR COMMITTEE, THE INTERESTED PERSON SHALL LEAVE THE BOARD OR COMMITTEE MEETING WHILE THE DETERMINATION OF A CONFLICT OF INTEREST IS DISCUSSED AND VOTED UPON BY THE REMAINING BOARD OR COMMITTEE MEMBERS. THE INTERESTED PERSON SHALL TAKE ALL NECESSARY ACTIONS TO ELIMINATE THE POTENTIAL CONFLICT OR OBTAIN A WRITTEN ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF THE CONFLICT FROM THE BOARD. ANY TRANSACTION OR ARRANGEMENT IN WHICH AN INDIVIDUAL HAS A MATERIAL INTEREST MAY ONLY BE MADE BY MAJORITY VOTE OF THE DISINTERESTED PARTICIPANTS WHEREBY: (I) THE TRANSACTION OR ARRANGEMENT IS IN THE CORPORATION'S BEST INTEREST AND FOR ITS OWN BENEFIT; (II) THE TRANSACTION IS FAIR AND REASONABLE TO THE CORPORATION AT THE TIME THE CORPORATION ENTERED INTO THE TRANSACTION; AND (III) PRIOR TO CONSUMMATING THE TRANSACTION OR ANY PART OF THEREOF, THE BOARD AUTHORIZED OR APPROVED THE TRANSACTION IN GOOD FAITH BY A VOTE OF A MAJORITY OF THE DIRECTORS THEN IN OFFICE WITHOUT COUNTING THE VOTE OF THE INTERESTED PERSON(S), AND WITH KNOWLEDGE OF THE MATERIAL FACTS CONCERNING THE TRANSACTION AND THE DIRECTOR'S INTEREST IN THE TRANSACTION, (IV) PRIOR TO APPROVAL, THE BOARD DETERMINES, IN GOOD FAITH AND AFTER REASONABLE INVESTIGATION, THAT THE CORPORATION COULD NOT HAVE OBTAINED A MORE ADVANTAGEOUS ARRANGEMENT WITH REASONABLE EFFORT UNDER THE CIRCUMSTANCES. ANY TRANSACTION BETWEEN THE CORPORATION AND ANOTHER ENTITY WITH A COMMON DIRECTOR SHALL BE MADE ONLY WHERE: (I) THE BOARD KNEW THE MATERIAL FACTS OF THE TRANSACTION AND OF THE COMMON DIRECTORSHIP; (II) THE BOARD, IN GOOD FAITH, APPROVED THE TRANSACTION WITHOUT THE VOTE OF THE COMMON DIRECTOR; AND (III) THE TRANSACTION IS JUST AND REASONABLE AS TO THE CORPORATION AT THE TIME THE BOARD APPROVED IT. IF APPROPRIATE, THE CHAIRPERSON OF THE BOARD OR COMMITTEE MAY APPOINT A DISINTERESTED PERSON OR COMMITTEE TO INVESTIGATE ALTERNATIVES TO THE PROPOSED TRANSACTION OR ARRANGEMENT AND EXERCISE DUE DILIGENCE TO DETERMINE WHETHER THE CORPORATION CAN OBTAIN A MORE ADVANTAGEOUS TRANSACTION OR ARRANGEMENT WITH REASONABLE EFFORTS FROM A PERSON OR ENTITY THAT WOULD NOT GIVE RISE TO A CONFLICT OF INTEREST. THE DISCLOSURES REQUIRED BY THIS POLICY SHALL BE MADE A MATTER OF RECORD IN THE MINUTES OF THE BOARD AND ALL COMMITTEES WITH BOARD DELEGATED POWERS AND SHALL CONTAIN: A. THE NAMES OF THE PERSONS WHO DISCLOSED A FINANCIAL INTEREST IN CONNECTION WITH AN ACTUAL OR POTENTIAL CONFLICT OF INTEREST, THE NATURE OF THE FINANCIAL INTEREST, ANY ACTION TAKEN TO DETERMINE WHETHER A CONFLICT OF INTEREST WAS PRESENT, AND THE BOARD'S OR COMMITTEE'S DECISION AS TO WHETHER A CONFLICT OF INTEREST IN FACT EXISTED; B. THE NAMES OF THE PERSONS WHO WERE PRESENT FOR DISCUSSIONS AND VOTES RELATING TO THE TRANSACTION OR ARRANGEMENT, THE CONTENT OF THE DISCUSSION, AND A RECORD OF ANY VOTES TAKEN IN CONNECTION THEREWITH. A VOTING MEMBER OF ANY COMMITTEE WHOSE JURISDICTION INCLUDES COMPENSATION MATTERS AND WHO RECEIVES COMPENSATION, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY FROM THE CORPORATION FOR SERVICES, SHALL BE PRECLUDED FROM VOTING ON MATTERS PERTAINING TO THAT MEMBER'S COMPENSATION. PHYSICIANS WHO RECEIVE COMPENSATION, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY, FROM THE CORPORATION, WHETHER AS EMPLOYEES OR INDEPENDENT CONTRACTORS, SHALL BE PRECLUDED FROM MEMBERSHIP ON ANY COMMITTEE WHOSE JURISDICTION INCLUDES COMPENSATION MATTERS. NO PHYSICIAN SHALL BE PROHIBITED FROM PROVIDING INFORMATION TO ANY COMMITTEE REGARDING PHYSICIAN COMPENSATION. PARTICIPANTS WHO FAIL TO DISCLOSE CONFLICTS OF INTEREST AS REQUIRED UNDER THIS POLICY OR WHO FAIL TO ELIMINATE SUCH CONFLICTS OR TO OBTAIN THE WAIVER OR APPROVAL THEREOF BY THE CORPORATION SHALL BE AFFORDED AN OPPORTUNITY TO EXPLAIN THE ALLEGED FAILURE TO DISCLOSE. IF THE CORPORATION DETERMINES THAT THE PARTICIPANT HAS IN FACT FAILED TO DISCLOSE AN ACTUAL OR POSSIBLE CONFLICT OF INTEREST, PARTICIPANT SHALL BE SUBJECT TO DISCIPLINARY ACTION, INCLUDING TERMINATION OR REMOVAL FROM OFFICE. IF THE BOARD OR A COMMITTEE HAS REASONABLE CAUSE TO BELIEVE THAT A MEMBER HAS FAILED TO DISCLOSE ACTUAL OR POSSIBLE CONFLICTS OF INTEREST, IT SHALL INFORM THE MEMBER OF THE BASIS FOR SUCH BELIEF AND AFFORD THE MEMBER AN OPPORTUNITY TO EXPLAIN THE ALLEGED FAILURE TO DISCLOSE. IF AFTER HEARING THE RESPONSE OF THE MEMBER AND MAKING SUCH FURTHER INVESTIGATION AS MAY BE WARRANTED BY THE CIRCUMSTANCES, THE BOARD OR COMMITTEE DETERMINES THAT THE MEMBER HAS IN FACT FAILED TO DISCLOSE AN ACTUAL OR POSSIBLE CONFLICT OF INTEREST, IT SHALL TAKE APPROPRIATE DISCIPLINARY AND CORRECTIVE ACTION INCLUDING DISMISSAL.
